title: ES6 Modules Check
description: Classify export/import statements as default or named.

questions.prompt: `export default function main() {}` is which kind of export?
questions.explanation: `export default` marks the module's single default export, whatever follows it (function, class, expression).

questions.prompt: `export { helper, util };` is which kind of export?
questions.explanation: Curly-brace `export { X }` declares one or more named exports — the importing side must use matching names in braces.

questions.prompt: `export const PI = 3.14;` is which kind of export?

options.text: Default export, because there's only one value
Named export — same import style as `export { PI }`

questions.explanation: `export const X`, `export let X`, `export function X`, and `export { X }` are all named exports — a module can have many of these.

questions.prompt: `import config from "./config.js";` (no curly braces) targets which kind of export?
questions.explanation: An import with no braces always targets the default export — the local name (`config`) can be anything, since there is only one default per module.

questions.prompt: `import { helper } from "./utils.js";` (with curly braces) targets which kind of export?

options.text: Nothing — braces are only for destructuring objects

questions.explanation: Braces on import always target a named export — the name inside the braces must match the exported name exactly (unless aliased with `as`).

questions.prompt: Can a single module have both a default export and named exports?

options.text: No, a module can only export one thing total
Yes — one default export plus any number of named exports
Yes, but only if they have the same name
No, default and named exports must live in separate files

questions.explanation: A module may have at most one default export, and separately, as many named exports as needed — they coexist in the same file.
